items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: Mrs. Donahue was a beautiful lady, she invited us out to her house for dinner

ctx.x: I says, “you’re kidding.” He says, “yeah, it was a temporary thing, it was shock like.” But he says but there’s still a little thing in the center of his eyes that had to clear up yet see? I said, “beautiful, man.” So I got him on the band. But he was like a real [scats]. So I said but you’ve got to play two/four. He says, “I don’t care I’ll play anything.” So anyway he comes on the band, now we’re in Boston, we’re playing, and the band was just fantastic, it was a great Dixieland band, but every time a trombone…

And I said Phil, we’re not trying to disrespect you or anything. This is how we feel. We’re young guys and we like to play, I mean we’ll play what you want, we’re playing for you, don’t we — we went through a long, long thing and I finally convinced him I said, “we love what you’re doing, we love playing with the band.
